---
title: "06.ARG_WHO_classification"
author: "Diego Coleto"
date: "2026-10-20"
output: html_document
---

Classification of every ResFinder variant according to the **WHO List of Medically Important Antimicrobials (MIA List, 2024)**,
the update of the WHO Critically Important Antimicrobials list (6th revision, 2019).

* Each variant is classified by the antibiotics in its ResFinder phenotype (`Data/Raw/Phenotypes/phenotypes.tsv`),
  mapped to WHO classes and categories with `Data/Raw/WHO/who_mia_2024_antibiotics.tsv`.
* A variant gets the highest category among its antibiotics:
  Human use only > HPCIA > CIA > HIA > IA > Not medically important.
  WHO states that classes authorized for human use only carry, at a minimum, an AMR risk similar to HPCIA.
* `who_critical` = Human use only, HPCIA or CIA; `who_highest_priority` = Human use only or HPCIA.
* Project decisions:
  - Resistance to anti-pseudomonal penicillins **without** a β-lactamase inhibitor (piperacillin, ticarcillin) does not
    make a gene critical; it is treated as HIA like the other penicillins. Otherwise narrow-spectrum penicillinases
    (e.g. TEM-1) would be critical. Combinations with inhibitors, 3rd/4th-generation cephalosporins, carbapenems and
    monobactams keep their WHO category.
  - Variants whose ResFinder phenotype is only "Unknown Beta-lactam" (e.g. cepA, cfxA, cfiA, OXA-347) stay Unclassified.
* Read-based CPMs (`cpm_gene_GPH.tsv`) are counted on gene families (`gene_family`, built by `00`), so a family
  stands for all its variants. A family is classified by the variants of the gene it is named after (e.g.
  `blaCTX-M-1` for the CTX-M-1 group), or by all its variants when no variant carries exactly that name
  (families named by a root or an alias, such as `blaTEM` or `dfrA7/17`). It is critical / highest priority if
  **most** of those variants are, so that a single variant cannot flip a whole family. Cluster-level
  columns report whether the cluster contains critical variants and in which proportion. Assembly-based hits
  (ABRicate on the full ResFinder database) are specific variants and use the variant-level classification.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())

library(tidyverse)
library(here)

category_levels <- c("Human use only", "HPCIA", "CIA", "HIA", "IA", "Not medically important", "Unclassified")
critical_categories <- c("Human use only", "HPCIA", "CIA")
```

# Load data

```{r load data}
phenotypes <- read_tsv(here("Data", "Raw", "Phenotypes", "phenotypes.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
clusters <- read_tsv(here("Data", "Processed", "phenotypes_cluster.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(gene, gene_family, cluster, is_representative)
who <- read_tsv(here("Data", "Raw", "WHO", "who_mia_2024_antibiotics.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Variant-level classification

```{r variant}
antibiotics_long <- phenotypes %>%
  select(gene, gene_base, Phenotype) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Phenotype, delim = regex("[,;]")) %>%
  mutate(antibiotic = str_squish(str_replace_all(Phenotype, "_", " "))) %>%
  filter(antibiotic != "") %>%
  left_join(who, by = "antibiotic") %>%
  # Project decision: anti-pseudomonal penicillins without inhibitor do not make a gene critical
  mutate(who_category = if_else(who_class == "Anti-pseudomonal penicillins", "HIA", who_category))

cat("Antibiotics without WHO mapping:", unique(antibiotics_long$antibiotic[is.na(antibiotics_long$who_category)]), "\n")
stopifnot(!anyNA(antibiotics_long$who_category))

variant_class <- antibiotics_long %>%
  mutate(who_category = factor(who_category, levels = category_levels)) %>%
  group_by(gene, gene_base) %>%
  summarise(antibiotics = paste(unique(antibiotic), collapse = "; "),
            who_classes = paste(unique(who_class[who_category %in% critical_categories]), collapse = "; "),
            who_category = levels(who_category)[min(as.integer(who_category))],
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(who_critical = who_category %in% critical_categories,
         who_highest_priority = who_category %in% c("Human use only", "HPCIA"),
         who_classes = na_if(who_classes, ""))

count(variant_class, who_category)
```

# Cluster-level classification

```{r cluster}
cluster_class <- variant_class %>%
  inner_join(clusters, by = "gene") %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(cluster_n_variants = n(),
            cluster_n_critical = sum(who_critical),
            cluster_frac_critical = mean(who_critical),
            cluster_who_category_max = category_levels[min(match(who_category, category_levels))],
            .groups = "drop")

arg_who <- variant_class %>%
  inner_join(clusters, by = "gene") %>%
  left_join(cluster_class, by = "cluster") %>%
  relocate(gene_family, cluster, is_representative, .after = gene_base)

stopifnot(nrow(arg_who) == nrow(phenotypes))
```

# Gene-family classification

```{r family}
family_class <- arg_who %>%
  group_by(gene_family) %>%
  mutate(named_variant = gene_base == gene_family,
         basis = if (any(named_variant)) "named gene" else "any variant") %>%
  filter(named_variant | basis == "any variant") %>%
  summarise(family_basis = first(basis),
            family_n_variants = n(),
            family_frac_critical = mean(who_critical),
            family_who_critical = family_frac_critical > 0.5,
            family_who_highest_priority = mean(who_highest_priority) > 0.5,
            .groups = "drop")

count(family_class, family_basis, family_who_critical)

# Families where "any variant critical" and "most variants critical" disagree
family_class %>% filter(family_frac_critical > 0, !family_who_critical) %>% arrange(desc(family_frac_critical))

# Families whose classification differs from that of their cluster representative (the previous unit)
arg_who %>%
  filter(is_representative) %>%
  distinct(gene_family, representative = gene_base, representative_critical = who_critical) %>%
  inner_join(family_class, by = "gene_family") %>%
  filter(representative_critical != family_who_critical) %>%
  select(gene_family, representative, representative_critical, family_who_critical, family_basis)

arg_who <- arg_who %>% left_join(family_class, by = "gene_family")
```

Clusters whose representative is not critical but that contain critical variants:

```{r heterogeneous clusters}
arg_who %>%
  filter(is_representative, !who_critical, cluster_n_critical > 0) %>%
  select(gene, who_category, cluster_n_variants, cluster_n_critical, cluster_who_category_max) %>%
  arrange(desc(cluster_n_critical))
```

# Agreement with the previous CIA list

`Data/Raw/Food_resistome/list_cia.txt` (gene names) is kept only for comparison.

```{r agreement}
old_cia <- read_tsv(here("Data", "Raw", "Food_resistome", "list_cia.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(gene_base = gene)

agreement <- variant_class %>%
  distinct(gene_base, who_critical) %>%
  group_by(gene_base) %>%
  summarise(who_critical = any(who_critical), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(in_old_list = gene_base %in% old_cia$gene_base)

count(agreement, in_old_list, who_critical)
```

# MASTER CIA gene list (Quijada et al. 2025)

`list_cia.txt` is byte-identical to `visualization_and_statistics/Figure_assembly_free/list_cia.txt` in the MASTER
repository, the gene list behind the CIA analyses of Quijada et al. (Nat Microbiol 2025). The paper describes it only
as AMRGs "conferring resistance to CIAs, selected according to previous publications" and does not define a
highest-priority subset, so none is derived here. It is a curated subset: it has no aminoglycoside, fosfomycin,
rifampicin or mupirocin genes, which the WHO 2024 list places in CIA or HPCIA. It is therefore kept as a
complementary, explicitly named classification ("MASTER CIA list"); the WHO classification stays primary.

Names are those of the 2022 ResFinder release. They are matched to `gene_base` in three steps, and nothing else is
inferred from partial names:

1. exact match;
2. case only (`oqxA`, `oqxB` became `OqxA`, `OqxB`);
3. allele renaming of `mcr-N`, whose alleles are now `mcr-N.M`; the list name is matched to every `mcr-N.M`
   variant (all of them carry the same gene, and ResFinder kept the gene number).

Entries left unmatched (van operon names, `crpP`, `mdf(A)`, `dldHA2X`) have no counterpart in the release used here
and are recorded as absent. `mcr-10` is newer than the list and is not added to it. A gene family is on the list when
most of the variants it is judged on (the same basis as the WHO family classification) are.

```{r master cia}
master_entries <- read_tsv(here("Data", "Raw", "Food_resistome", "list_cia.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(list_gene = gene, list_class = Family)

variant_names <- arg_who %>% distinct(gene, gene_base, gene_family, who_category, who_critical)

match_entry <- function(name) {
  exact <- variant_names %>% filter(gene_base == name)
  if (nrow(exact) > 0) return(mutate(exact, match_type = "exact"))
  by_case <- variant_names %>% filter(tolower(gene_base) == tolower(name))
  if (nrow(by_case) > 0) return(mutate(by_case, match_type = "alias: case"))
  if (str_detect(name, "^mcr-\\d+$")) {
    alleles <- variant_names %>% filter(str_detect(gene_base, paste0("^", fixed(name), "\\.\\d+$")))
    if (nrow(alleles) > 0) return(mutate(alleles, match_type = "alias: allele renaming"))
  }
  tibble(match_type = "absent")
}

master_mapping <- master_entries %>%
  mutate(hits = map(list_gene, match_entry)) %>%
  unnest(hits) %>%
  mutate(classification = if_else(match_type == "absent", NA_character_, "MASTER CIA list"),
         source = "list_cia.txt (MASTER; Quijada et al. 2025)",
         decision = if_else(match_type == "absent",
                            "Not mapped: no counterpart in the ResFinder release used",
                            "Variant on the MASTER CIA list")) %>%
  select(list_gene, list_class, match_type, gene, gene_base, gene_family, classification, source,
         who_category, who_critical, decision)

# A variant matched by two list entries of different class would be ambiguous
ambiguous <- master_mapping %>% filter(!is.na(gene)) %>% group_by(gene) %>% filter(n_distinct(list_class) > 1)
cat("Ambiguous variants:", nrow(ambiguous), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(ambiguous) == 0)

count(master_mapping %>% distinct(list_gene, match_type), match_type)

listed_variants <- master_mapping %>% filter(!is.na(gene)) %>% distinct(gene) %>% pull(gene)

family_master <- arg_who %>%
  mutate(master_listed = gene %in% listed_variants) %>%
  group_by(gene_family) %>%
  mutate(named_variant = gene_base == gene_family,
         basis = if (any(named_variant)) "named gene" else "any variant") %>%
  filter(named_variant | basis == "any variant") %>%
  summarise(family_basis = first(basis),
            family_n_variants = n(),
            family_n_master_listed = sum(master_listed),
            family_frac_master_listed = mean(master_listed),
            family_master_cia = family_frac_master_listed > 0.5,
            family_who_critical = first(family_who_critical),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(decision = case_when(
    family_master_cia & family_who_critical ~ "MASTER CIA and WHO critical",
    family_master_cia ~ "MASTER CIA only",
    family_who_critical & family_n_master_listed > 0 ~ "WHO critical; MASTER-listed variants are a minority",
    family_who_critical ~ "WHO critical only",
    family_n_master_listed > 0 ~ "Neither; MASTER-listed variants are a minority",
    TRUE ~ "Neither"))

count(family_master, family_master_cia, family_who_critical)
```

# Save

```{r save}
write_tsv(arg_who, here("Data", "Processed", "arg_who_classification.tsv"))
write_tsv(master_mapping, here("Data", "Processed", "arg_cia_list_mapping.tsv"))
write_tsv(family_master, here("Data", "Processed", "arg_family_master_cia.tsv"))
```
